title: Zesty Iron-Seared Ethiopian Oats Doro Wot
description: A hearty, one-pot Ethiopian Doro Wot dish made with oats, featuring a zesty iron-seared crust and a paleo-friendly twist.
instructions: Heat 1 tablespoon of ghee in an iron teppan over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.
Add the chicken thighs and cook until browned on both sides, about 5 minutes per side.
Add the turmeric, cumin, paprika, salt, and black pepper, and stir to combine.
Add the berbere spice mix and stir to combine.
Add the rolled oats and water, and stir to combine.
Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to low and simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.
Remove the lid and cook for an additional 10 minutes, or until the oats have absorbed most of the liquid and the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the chopped cilantro and serve hot.
Serve the Zesty Iron-Seared Ethiopian Oats Doro Wot hot, garnished with additional cilantro if desired.
This dish can be made in advance and refrigerated or frozen for later use.
Reheat the dish over low heat, stirring occasionally, until hot and steaming.
Serve with injera bread or over rice, if desired.
Note: Traditionally, Doro Wot is made with eggs, but this version uses oats as a paleo-friendly substitute.
To make this dish more substantial, add diced vegetables such as carrots or potatoes to the pot during the last 10 minutes of cooking.
This recipe makes 4-6 servings and can be easily doubled or tripled for a larger crowd.
The iron teppan is a must-have for this recipe, as it provides a crispy, well-browned crust on the outside of the oats.
If you don't have an iron teppan, you can make this recipe in a large skillet or Dutch oven, but the results will be slightly different.
The berbere spice mix is a key ingredient in this recipe, so be sure to use a high-quality mix or make your own from scratch.
